lines.title: This is pi-account-guard. Rotate accounts freely, and never send a turn into the wrong zone.
lines.intro: Many of us use a work account and a personal account in the same pi. Here, pi is open in my dotfiles, a personal repository, but the selected model is GPT-5.5, on the company's OpenAI key. The footer already warns about it.
lines.block-ask: Let's ask what install dot sh does.
lines.block: Before anything is sent, pi-account-guard checks the account against this place. An account is a provider plus where its key comes from, here the OPENAI underscore API underscore KEY variable. That account is tagged work, and this repository is personal. So the turn is blocked, and nothing reaches the company's OpenAI account.
lines.switch-offer: The fix is one keystroke away. The first choice switches to Claude Sonnet, on my personal Anthropic key.
lines.switch-done: The same prompt runs again on Claude, and the footer shows a match.
lines.tag-intro: Accounts start untagged. Let's switch to Gemini Flash, on a Google key the guard has never seen, and ask for a git alias.
lines.tag-prompt: Before the turn goes, the guard asks which zones this Google account belongs to. Nothing is ticked for you.
lines.tag-done: We tick personal. The turn goes at once, and the tag is saved for next time.
lines.rotate-intro: Rotators and routers switch accounts on their own, sometimes in the middle of a turn. Let's ask for a long review of my zshrc, then switch to GPT-5.5 while it streams.
lines.rotate-block: The guard catches the change and stops the turn at once. It is aborted, not finished on the work account.
lines.rotate-offer: Once pi is idle, the account it was on comes first. There is no allow once here, because the aborted turn is gone. We switch back to Gemini.
lines.status-place: Finally, slash guard shows what the guard sees. This directory matches no place rule, so it falls to the default zone, personal.
lines.status-account: The Google account is tagged personal, so it matches, and turns here go through.
lines.end: To install it, run the command on screen. Then try slash guard tour, or add your first place rule.
